title: Dispatch queue backlog runbook
brief: Quickpost Couriers' Dispatch team needs an on-call runbook for when the dispatch-jobs queue backs up, owned by Dispatch Engineering. Sections: "Symptoms", "Diagnose", "Fix steps" and "Escalation". Symptoms: the QUEUE_DEPTH_HIGH alert fires when depth stays above 5000 for 10 minutes (normal is under 400), and drivers see new jobs arrive late in the app. Diagnose: check the queue depth and consumer count with kubectl -n dispatch get hpa dispatch-consumer, look at the oldest message age on the queue dashboard, and check the database connection pool, which is capped at 200 connections. Fix steps, in order, with sub-steps. 1 Scale the consumers: a) run kubectl -n dispatch scale deploy dispatch-consumer --replicas=24, b) wait 5 minutes and re-check, c) if depth is still rising, scale to 40, which is the maximum the database pool supports. 2 Check for poison messages: a) if one message has been retried more than 10 times, b) move it to dispatch-dlq with the dlq-move tool. 3 Pause the bulk import scheduler in the admin console, because bulk imports add up to 3000 jobs at a time. 4 When depth drops under 400, re-enable the scheduler gradually. Readers must be told firmly never to purge dispatch-jobs, because every message is a real customer delivery. Escalation: if depth is still above 5000 after 20 minutes, page the Dispatch Engineering lead and open an incident in #incidents.

edit.request: Scale to 30 replicas instead of 24 in the first step, and raise the alert threshold from 5000 to 8000 everywhere.
